statement: Quaternion kinematics describes the continuous-time evolution of an orientation quaternion under angular velocity, defined by the differential equation \dot{\mathbf{q}} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{q} \otimes \mathbf{\omega} (for body-frame angular velocity \mathbf{\omega}) or \dot{\mathbf{q}} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{\omega} \otimes \mathbf{q} (for spatial/inertial-frame angular velocity). The supplied source [wikipedia:Quaternions_and_spatial_rotation] does not support this concept and genuinely contains nothing to derive regarding quaternion kinematics; it covers only static rotation matrices, axis-angle conversions, rotation composition, and optimization derivatives of rotated vectors with respect to quaternion components.

symbols.meaning: time derivative of the orientation quaternion
skew-symmetric 4x4 matrix representation of angular velocity

assumptions.assumption: The attitude quaternion maintains unit norm (\|\mathbf{q}\| = 1) along its trajectory.
assumptions.breaks_when: Discrete-time numerical integration causes norm drift away from the unit sphere.

assumptions.assumption: The angular velocity vector \mathbf{\omega} is expressed in the body-fixed reference frame.
assumptions.breaks_when: Angular velocity is resolved in the inertial/world frame, requiring the reversed multiplication order \dot{\mathbf{q}} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{\omega} \otimes \mathbf{q}.

failure_modes.signature: Supplied source contains no differential equations, angular velocity, or time derivatives.
failure_modes.cause: The supplied source [wikipedia:Quaternions_and_spatial_rotation] discusses spatial rotation algebra and static optimization derivatives, omitting time-dependent rotational kinematics.
Accumulated truncation and finite-precision roundoff errors in numerical integration without continuous re-normalization.

failure_modes.signature: Incorrect rotation trajectory or inverted rotation axis.
failure_modes.cause: Conflating body-frame angular velocity (post-multiplication) with spatial-frame angular velocity (pre-multiplication).

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so quaternion_kinematics is recorded as a definition
